skill.name: quantall-mcp
skill.description: Run local A-share factor analysis, strategy backtests, IC studies, stock screening, and visual exploration through the QuantAll MCP engine.
skill.summary: Use a local vectorized engine to analyze A-share market data and manage an optional DuckDB dataset.
skill.author: mifochen

security_audit.summary: All static pattern alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, loopback addresses, scoped configuration writes, fixed subprocess arguments, or normal DuckDB access. Semantic review found high-risk sandbox-bypass guidance, unauditable Python execution, unverified remote installation, and SQL injection. Plaintext API token storage adds a medium-risk credential exposure.

remediation.issue: Installation guidance recommends disabling the sandbox.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the bypass instruction and fix the conflicting file workflow within normal sandbox permissions.

remediation.issue: The local Python execution engine is not included for audit.
remediation.suggestion: Publish the engine source and enforce an AST allowlist inside an isolated worker without filesystem, network, import, or subprocess access.

remediation.issue: Remote quantall installation lacks version and hash verification.
remediation.suggestion: Install an exact reviewed version with hashes from a trusted index, and remove guidance that upgrades to unspecified releases.

remediation.issue: Stock query parameters are interpolated into SQL.
remediation.suggestion: Use DuckDB parameters for every value and validate symbols and dates against strict formats before executing queries.

remediation.issue: The Tushare token is stored in plaintext.
remediation.suggestion: Read the token from a protected secret provider or environment variable, and never create a credential file with default permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Sandbox Bypass Guidance
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` when installation conflicts occur. This removes a security boundary instead of resolving the underlying file operation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The bypass setting is stated directly as an installation workaround on line 73.

semantic_findings.title: AI-Generated Python Execution Is Not Auditable
semantic_findings.description: The core workflow executes AI-authored Python snippets through QuantAll. Only prompt-level restrictions are visible, while the external engine enforcing them is absent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly describes local Python execution and behavioral restrictions. The repository does not contain the QuantAll engine implementation needed to verify isolation.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Package Installation Without Integrity Verification
semantic_findings.description: Installation fetches quantall without a version or hash. Upgrade guidance requests the latest release from a remote mirror, allowing unreviewed code changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented pip commands omit both a version constraint and hashes, and the upgrade command explicitly selects newer remote content.

semantic_findings.title: SQL Injection in Stock Query Tools
semantic_findings.description: MCP parameters for symbols and dates are interpolated directly into DuckDB SQL. Crafted values can change query structure and access or modify local data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both MCP tools concatenate unsanitized string parameters into executable SQL before passing it to DuckDB.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Tushare API Token Storage
semantic_findings.description: Update tools direct users to store a Tushare API token in API_tushare.txt. The script reads the secret without access controls or protected storage.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The tool documentation and implementation explicitly create and read API_tushare.txt as the credential source.

content.value_statement: Large A-share datasets make factor testing and strategy validation slow and inconsistent. QuantAll runs vectorized local analysis and returns measurable backtest, IC, screening, and visualization results.
actual_capabilities: Runs vectorized strategy backtests with return, Sharpe ratio, drawdown, and win-rate summaries.
Calculates single or batch factor IC metrics and factor correlations.
Screens A-share stocks with vectorized conditions and set operations.
Builds heat maps, weighted views, and visual layers from market data.
Creates, configures, queries, and updates an optional local DuckDB market database.
limitations: Requires a local Python environment and the external quantall package.
Results depend on the coverage, freshness, and correctness of the configured market database.
Optional database updates require network access and a Tushare API credential.
The tools support research workflows and do not place trades or provide financial advice.

use_cases.title: Validate a Trading Hypothesis
use_cases.description: Backtest entry and exit rules across A-share history, then compare returns, drawdowns, and win rates.

use_cases.title: Compare Candidate Factors
use_cases.description: Measure IC, IR, and correlations for several factors before selecting complementary signals.

use_cases.title: Maintain Local Market Data
use_cases.description: Create or update a DuckDB dataset and configure the QuantAll engine to use it.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Available Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the QuantAll service and list available fields. Summarize the date range, stock coverage, and missing data before analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Backtest a Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Backtest my stated entry and exit rules with close and next-open execution. Report returns, Sharpe ratio, drawdown, win rate, and assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Multiple Factors
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these factors across the same period and universe: [factors]. Report IC, IR, stability, correlations, and redundant signals.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Robust Research Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [hypothesis] across [universe] and [period]. Check data availability, prevent lookahead bias, compare parameter ranges, and explain unstable results.

output_examples.input: Test whether smaller market capitalization predicts stronger next-month returns.
output: Coverage summary with the tested universe, dates, and missing-data exclusions.
Factor report with IC direction, stability, quantile spread, and benchmark comparison.
Conclusion that separates measured evidence from interpretation and limitations.

output_examples.input: Backtest a moving-average crossover and compare close execution with next-open execution.
output: Side-by-side performance summary for both execution assumptions.
Return, drawdown, Sharpe ratio, win rate, turnover, and holding-period comparison.
Warnings about lookahead bias, data gaps, and sensitivity to parameters.

output_examples.input: Find low-valuation stocks with improving profitability and inspect their industry distribution.
output: Filtered stock set with each criterion stated clearly.
Data timestamp, field definitions, and excluded records.

best_practices: Obtain explicit approval before installing packages, changing MCP configuration, starting services, or creating files.
Call available_data before analysis and use only documented vectorized operations.
State the universe, dates, execution assumptions, data gaps, and lookahead controls in every result.
anti_patterns: Do not disable the sandbox or weaken host protections to complete installation.
Do not install unspecified package versions or upgrade remote code without review.
Do not run parallel tools, assume field names, or expose oversized detail outputs directly.

faq.answer: It targets mainland China A-share data available in the configured QuantAll database.

faq.question: Does the skill require installation?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a local Python environment, the quantall package, MCP configuration, and a local service.

faq.question: Does it use the internet?
faq.answer: The analysis service is local. Installation, upgrades, and optional market-data updates use external services.

faq.question: Is UpdateStock required?
faq.answer: No. UpdateStock is optional when an existing DuckDB database or the bundled test data is sufficient.

faq.question: Can it place trades?
faq.answer: No. It performs research, screening, factor analysis, visualization, and backtesting only.

faq.question: How should sensitive credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use protected secret storage and restrict access. Avoid storing API tokens in plaintext files.
